To my understanding a Kickstarter campaign requires the receiving company to be registered in the US and subscribe to their laws. If WhoaVerse wants to uphold its values against censorship it can not become a US based company; otherwise, if WhoaVerse gets traction we will see the same ordeal we had to witness over at reddit with unexplained behaviour of admins planting mods in big subreddits to enforce censorship of various degrees. The fact that right now in none of the biggest subreddits you can post anything at all about the NSA, FBI, Obama administration or even link to an article of The Intercept without getting your post deleted or even shadow banned, is, for me, the strongest possible argument not to register WhoaVerse as US company and start a Kickstarter campaign.

A campaign on a site like IndieGoGo on the other hand might be worth looking into. If you want someone to back such a campaign you need to remind people why they might want to migrate away from other sites to WhoaVerse. [1]

The next thing you need is exposure, which is gained by not just getting the press to notice your campaign but also convince some of them that your campaign is worth writing about. [2]

Long explanations in funding campaigns rarely work as far as I know, so I wouldn't try to describe the entire concept that you have of WhoaVerse but rather connect what people know with what people want to have/change. Oh and you need to clearly address that WhoaVerse looks a lot like reddit and why that is and how this is not just a clone that will end up the same horrible way.

Good luck.
